5 inspiring cases of successful influencer marketing campaigns

By Rhonda Martinez | November 18, 2019

The days when TV advertising used to be the most effective marketing tool are long gone. These days, we are facing a new era of marketing where influencers are [taking over traditional marketing tools and strategies](https://www.agilitypr.com/pr-news/public-relations/as-influencer-marketing-gets-more-sophisticated-comms-pros-expand-strategy-investments/). Collaborating with an influencer who has a fan base of loyal followers relevant to a product has proven to be successful and efficient. Nowadays, more and more world-renowned brands turn to influencers to [promote their brands](https://www.agilitypr.com/pr-news/public-relations/4-critical-steps-to-creating-an-effective-influencer-marketing-strategy/).

Why? Followers treat their influencers like friends. That is why as soon as a famous blogger starts using some product or talking about one, thousands of followers are ready to try the product themselves. In 2019, influencers posted approximately [4.9 million #ads on Instagram](https://www.wired.com/story/inside-the-industry-social-media-influence/), and that number includes only those that are properly disclosed.

Actually, the numbers speak for themselves: if brands are ready to pay thousands of dollars so that an [influencer mentions their product/service](https://www.agilitypr.com/pr-news/public-relations/as-influencer-marketing-matures-are-influencers-own-motivations-changing/), it means that it’s really working. That is why we’ve decided to examine 5 inspiring cases of such successful influencer marketing campaigns.

## 1\. Edubirdie

More than 250 popular YouTube Channels and more than [700 million views](https://www.theverge.com/2018/5/6/17324856/youtube-removed-hundreds-of-videos-promoted-edubirdie-academic-cheating-service). Can you just imagine this number? This scandalous YouTube marketing campaign has brought EduBirdie thousands of loyal customers and made some serious waves in social media. This is all thanks to the idea of using social media influencers and some famous YouTube personalities and popular channels (HoomanTV, To Catch A Cheater, Coby Persin, Zias, and others) to promote essay-writing services through short shout-out ads within the YouTube content.

The company targeted students through YouTube channels that cover pranks, dating, gaming, music, fashion, and dozens of other categories – everything an average college student might be interested in. While EduBirdie targeted students by their interests, the company didn’t make any strict rules on how to present itself on YouTube, so influencers had absolute freedom to present this platform the way they saw it. And even though the ads were brief (10 to 30 seconds shout-outs), this marketing company went through the roof and had great success.

![5 inspiring cases of successful influencer marketing campaigns](https://www.agilitypr.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/rhonda1.png)

Zias (with 3.1 million subscribers) promoting EduBirdie on their YouTube channel

The campaign has drawn so much attention that the BBC published its own investigation revealing the scale of the marketing campaign and a number of YouTube influencers involved in it. As it turned out, EduBirdie’s ads were violating YouTube’s Academic Aid policy. As a result, YouTube has taken down hundreds of YouTube videos (some of those had tens of millions of views) that mentioned the EduBirdie platform and other companies.

“The situation became so resonant that even PayPal was asked to take measures regarding the payment processing services for such companies. As a result, since April 4, 2019, PayPal itself has claimed that it will no longer be providing services to essay writing companies”, says Adam Simon, a blogger and owner of an [essay writing services review site](https://legitwritingservices.com/).

Despite the problem that occurred, the figures remain the same, and EduBirdie has received wide coverage in the media. People were actively talking about this situation for months, resulting in making the name of the company even more recognizable.

## 2\. Fiji Water

Healthy lifestyle is the thing that makes thousands of brands rich today. This water brand turned to instagram influencer Danielle Bernstein (2.2 million followers) to promote their product. Danielle is a fashion blogger, so the target audience was clearly defined: women whose aim was to have a good look, nice body and a healthy lifestyle. Together with the blogger they’ve created a promotional campaign, wherein Denielle would promote a brand in unobtrusive way. She would occasionally make promotional posts on Instagram and appear in public with a bottle of Fiji water in hand. The gist of the promo was to offer viewers 8-minute workout videos with Danielle and her personal coach. This marketing technique was truly efficient as it appealed to followers through their desire to look like Danielle. To do so they need to keep fit, and Fiji Water is going to help them stay hydrated. Voila, this is how you get your brand boosted.

![5 inspiring cases of successful influencer marketing campaigns](https://www.agilitypr.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/rhonda2.png)

These days H&M is among the brands having the largest audience of followers on Instagram. All because of the thoughtful advertising campaign they’ve created. # Influencer Marketing Agency in Turkey

House of Lein is an influencer marketing agency based in Istanbul. We help international brands reach Turkish audiences through creators they already trust, and we run the campaign end to end: creator matching, briefs, contracts, local disclosure rules, publishing and reporting.

[Request a proposal →](https://www.houseoflein.com/#iletisim)[info@houseoflein.com](mailto:info@houseoflein.com)

## What we do

| Service | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| Creator matching | Finding Turkish creators by audience fit, engagement quality and brand fit, not follower count |
| Campaign management | Briefs, contracts, product seeding, approvals, publishing schedule and reporting |
| UGC production | Creator-made, user-style content for your ads, product pages and social channels |
| Creative strategy | Goals, audience insight, message, creator portfolio, platforms and measurement plan |
| Local compliance | Making sure every post follows Turkish disclosure rules |

## Why Turkey?

Turkey has a large, young and highly social audience, with tens of millions of people on social platforms. Shopping decisions are strongly shaped by recommendations, and creators play a central role in how people discover products, places and brands.

## How we work with international brands

1.  **Brief in English:** We start from your goals, markets and brand guidelines.
2.  **Local translation of the idea:** We adapt the message so it feels native to Turkish audiences rather than translated.
3.  **Creator shortlist:** We propose creators with audience data and the reasoning behind each choice.
4.  **Contracts and compliance:** We handle local contracts, usage rights, exclusivity and disclosure labels.
5.  **Reporting in English:** Results are reported by creator and content against the goals set at the start.

## Our offices

House of Lein has two offices in Istanbul: in Etiler (Beşiktaş) and in Ataşehir. Write to us at [info@houseoflein.com](mailto:info@houseoflein.com); our Turkish pages are available under [Hizmetler](https://www.houseoflein.com/hizmetler).

## Frequently asked questions

### Why work with a local agency in Turkey?

+

Turkish audiences respond to creators who speak their language and culture. A local agency knows the creator landscape, negotiates in Turkish, handles local contracts and payments, and makes sure every post follows Turkish advertising disclosure rules.

### What are the disclosure rules for influencer ads in Turkey?

+

Under the advertising regulation in force since 1 August 2026, posts made in return for any benefit must carry the word 'Reklam' (advertisement) or 'Tanıtım' (promotion) together with the advertiser's name, visible at first glance. Gifted products and invitations also count as a benefit.

### Which platforms matter most in Turkey?

+

Most influencer collaborations in Turkey run on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube; LinkedIn is increasingly used for B2B brands.

### Do you work in English?

+

Yes. We brief, report and communicate with your team in English, and work with creators and partners in Turkish.

## Let's create together.

Tell us about your brand and goals; we will come back with a plan.
